issues.legal_issue: A landlord holding a life interest and receiving rent as trustee may seek eviction for bona fide demolition and reconstruction, and a possible dispute with remaindermen does not bar adjudication of that claim against the tenants.
material_facts: The landlord held a life interest in the premises under a settlement and was entitled to receive its rent.
The Rent Controller found the landlord’s requirement for demolition and reconstruction bona fide and ordered eviction.
The appellate authority rejected eviction because the landlord held only a life interest, and the tenants argued that demolition could prejudice the remaindermen.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was within the statutory definition of landlord and could seek eviction for demolition and reconstruction; any rights between the landlord and remaindermen had to be worked out in appropriate proceedings and did not affect the tenant proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(6) and 14(1)(b) of the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, respectively include within “landlord” a person entitled to receive rent as trustee and permit recovery where the building is bona fide required for demolition to erect a new building. The Act is a self-contained and complete code governing landlord-tenant rights, as recognized in M/s Raval and Co. v. K. G. Ramachandra and others; a dispute with persons who are not tenants under the Act does not determine the landlord’s claim against the tenants.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.claimant_receives_rent_as_trustee: The claimant was entitled to receive rent from the premises as a trustee.
predicates.bona_fide_demolition_reconstruction_requ: The building was found to be bona fide required for demolition and reconstruction.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings an eviction proceeding, receives rent as trustee, and has a bona fide demolition-and-reconstruction requirement, the landlord may seek eviction for reconstruction despite holding only a life interest.

issues.legal_issue: A single eviction petition is maintainable for two tenancies in the same premises when the tenancy is one.
material_facts: The eviction claim concerned two tenancies in the same premises, one for residential use and one for non-residential use.
The tenants objected that a single petition covering both was not maintainable.
The court treated the tenancy as one.
issues.conclusion: A single petition was maintainable because the tenancy was one.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that there was no substance in the objection where the two tenancies in the same premises constituted one tenancy.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.two_use_based_tenancies_same_premises: The eviction claim covered residential and non-residential tenancies in the same premises.
predicates.tenancy_is_one: The two tenancies were treated as one tenancy.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding covers residential and non-residential tenancies in the same premises that constitute one tenancy, one petition is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Demolition and reconstruction by a landlord are not inherently mala fide when undertaken to improve the property’s business prospects or returns.
material_facts: The tenants argued that demolition and reconstruction by a landlord holding a life interest would per se be mala fide because it could prejudice the remaindermen.
The Rent Controller had found the landlord’s requirement bona fide.
issues.conclusion: Demolishing the property to build a new structure for improving business or obtaining better returns cannot, by itself, be characterized as mala fide.
issues.legal_principle: A landlord may demolish a property and erect a new structure to improve the landlord’s business or obtain better returns on the investment; that purpose does not by itself make the landlord’s conduct mala fide.

predicates.tenant_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.landlord_seeks_demolition_and_reconstruc: The landlord sought possession to demolish the building and erect a new structure.
predicates.purpose_is_business_improvement_or_bette: The proposed new structure was intended to improve business or obtain better returns on the investment.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding, when a landlord seeks demolition and reconstruction to improve business or returns, that purpose alone does not make the demolition and reconstruction mala fide.
